name: Vase / spiral wall
summary: A single continuous helical wall from a base diameter to a top diameter — vase/spiral-vase mode, with an optional linear taper.

evidence.label: EXPERIMENTAL
evidence.scope: Deterministic generator validated by schema, geometry-bounds, and golden-output tests. Not yet evidenced on physical hardware under this exact manifest and generator revision. The capability it depends on (planar-motion) is itself ROBOT-CONFIRMED on the reference machine from extensive prior print history — this operation's own EXPERIMENTAL label is about this specific generator revision, not about whether the underlying motion is achievable at all.

baseOuterDiameter.description: Diameter at the wall's own bottom (z = zStart).

topOuterDiameter.description: Diameter at the wall's own top (z = zStart + height). Equal to baseOuterDiameter for a straight (non-tapered) vase wall.

height.description: Total rise of just this wall, not including whatever it's built on top of.

zStart.description: Z height this wall begins at — typically the top of a solid base built by a preceding layer-filling invocation.

dependencyNotes: Not a hard runtime dependency of the generator itself, which only needs zStart. Documents the intended composition: a plan typically invokes layer-filling first to build a solid or perimeter-only base, then this operation continues upward from that base's own top Z as one continuous single wall — no separate inner perimeter, no infill, by definition of vase/spiral mode.

validation.description: Every emitted point's radius stays within [min(baseOuterDiameter, topOuterDiameter), max(...)] / 2; z stays within [zStart, zStart + height].

Z rises continuously point-to-point within each revolution rather than stepping between flat layers — an ordinary planar (XY) ring motion that simply never resets Z to a constant, not a heightfield surface like non-planar-cladding.
Exactly one path family (Spiral wall); no separate perimeter or infill paths, by definition of vase/spiral mode.

Emits a `warnings` entry when the requested taper implies a per-revolution radial shift steeper than the general ~45deg unsupported-overhang guideline used across FDM printing generally — a general guideline, not evidence from this project's own hardware. See README.md.
